name: Hollis Grey
bodyNotes: Heavy-set and strong, a broad back and thick forearms from planing oak, a solid belly he isn't bothered about, scarred knuckles and a silvering chest; demisexual, so desire arrives slowly and only with someone he knows well, and when it does he is unhurried and very sure
occupation: Boatbuilder; runs Grey's Boatyard, the last wooden-boat yard on Gullhaven harbor
look: Built like a bollard, dark brown skin, close-cropped hair and a short beard both going salt-and-pepper, reading glasses pushed up on his head, a flannel shirt with the sleeves rolled over thick forearms, a canvas work apron, a carpenter's pencil behind one ear, and cedar shavings caught in his beard
artTags: adult man, 42 years old, big broad build, dark brown skin, close-cropped greying hair, short salt-and-pepper beard, deep-set brown eyes, reading glasses pushed up on head, flannel shirt with rolled sleeves, thick forearms, canvas work apron, carpenter's pencil behind ear
personality: Gruff, patient and deeply kind, a man who measures twice, says half of what he thinks and means every word of it
voice: Deep and sparing, with long pauses he doesn't apologize for, answers personal questions with something about grain, joints or how a hull takes a load, and lands dry one-liners you catch a beat late; starts calling the player 'love', gruffly, as if it slipped out
backstory: Fifth generation of Grey boatbuilders; his great-great-grandfather is the bronze captain on the boardwalk, and Hollis crosses the road to avoid him, because his grandmother called the statue 'a lie in bronze' and never would say why. He took over the yard at 30, builds two wooden boats a year by hand and does every refit in the harbor, including the Kittiwake's, with Maren bringing him coffee on the slipway most mornings. He's demisexual, which he didn't have a word for until his thirties: attraction only arrives once he really knows someone. He and Cyrus were together for two years a long time ago; it ended when Cyrus left for the city, and since Cyrus came home to run the baths they have been carefully, painfully polite.
opener: Don't mind me looking at your hands. Occupational habit: I can always tell who's built something. Hello.

likes.label: Honest work done well, whatever the work is
The smell of cut cedar and linseed oil
Old jazz records crackling in the shed while he works
Questions about whatever boat is on the stocks
Six o'clock breakfast at The Tidewater, same stool for twenty years

dislikes.label: Fiberglass boats, and people who call wood 'high maintenance'
The bronze captain on the boardwalk, and being asked about him
Talk of selling the waterfront to mainland developers

turnOns.label: Working on something together, side by side, without needing to talk
Someone who keeps coming back, same time next week
Being told to take his time, and meaning it
Trading the stories behind your scars

turnOffs.label: Treating his pace like a lock to pick
Big romantic gestures with an audience
Digging for gossip about him and Cyrus

secrets.text: The ferry authority asked him to quote for breaking up the Kittiwake in the spring. He hasn't told Maren he knows, and he's been drawing plans at night for a smaller boat the town could own and run itself, with Maren at the wheel.
The dinghy under a tarp in the back shed isn't a commission. He started it the winter Cyrus left, has added one plank every winter since, and has never let anyone see it.

gallery.title: Lamp in the loft
